requirements.evidence: Core flow is implemented: members page is manager-only (`app/Livewire/Entity/Members.php:51` mount authorizes `update`), invite form validates `required|email:strict|max:255` and `Rule::in(ASSIGNABLE_ROLES)` (`Members.php:64-67`), duplicate-member/pending checks (`:78`, `:89`), race -> error on `inviteEmail` (`:124-127`), rate limit only on success (`:96-104`, `:140`), queued mail (`:131`), `EntityInvite` model with lowercase/trimmed email mutator and `pending()` scope (`app/Models/EntityInvite.php:56-60`, `:77-81`), migration with unique `(entity_id,email)` and cascade FK, `EntityInviteMail` with `markdown: 'emails.entity-invite'`, switcher/onboarding placement (`resources/views/entity/switcher.blade.php:8`, `create-entity.blade.php:18`). Gaps: the required single `@error('inviteEmail')` element is absent from the invite form (only `@error('inviteRole')` at `resources/views/livewire/entity/members.blade.php:29`), no `routes/` change for the route-level 403, accepted invites are deleted rather than only expired ones (`Members.php:107-117`), and the owner-membership 403 path is unreachable from the UI (`Members.php:174`, `:183-192`).

conventions.evidence: Migrations have a reversible `down()` (`database/migrations/2026_10_29_000000_create_entity_invites_table.php:31-34`), fillable is explicit (`app/Models/EntityInvite.php:13`), Blade/Bulma markup is semantic with labels and no `{!! !!}`. But domain writes stay inline in Livewire instead of `app/Actions/*` (`Members.php:71-143`, `app/Livewire/Entity/PendingInvites.php:33-55`), no docs/CHANGELOG updates at all although conventions.md:92-103 require `docs/database-schema.md`, `docs/business-rules.md` and `CHANGELOG.md`, and validation uses an inline rules array instead of the project's `#[Validate]` + `$this->validate()` pattern (`Members.php:64-69`, `:183-185`; the `Validate` import was dropped).

security.evidence: Every public action authorizes server-side: `sendInvite`/`cancelInvite`/`openMember`/`saveRole`/`confirmRemoval` call `$this->authorize('update', $this->entity)` (`Members.php:147`, `:162`, `:179`, `:215`) and IDs are re-resolved through `$this->entity->invites()`/`memberships()` (`:149`, `:187`); `accept`/`decline` check the invitee e-mail case-insensitively before acting (`PendingInvites.php:21-28`, `:72-79`); input is validated (`Members.php:64-67`, `:183-185`) and all output uses `{{ }}`. Remaining low-impact gaps: an already-accepted invite can be deleted via `decline` (`PendingInvites.php:81`), and invite IDs are resolved globally before the 403 (`PendingInvites.php:21`, `:72`).

tests.evidence: `change.diff` contains no `tests/` file at all (18 changed paths, all app/lang/view/migration/factory); the new `sendInvite`, `cancelInvite`, `openMember`, `saveRole`, `confirmRemoval`, `removeMember` and `accept`/`decline` endpoints ship with zero Pest/PHPUnit coverage, so there are no happy-path, validation, unauthorized-call or tamper tests as conventions.md:12-20 and :176-185 require.

simplicity.evidence: Good reuse: the model owns normalization and a `pending()` scope (`EntityInvite.php:56-60`, `:77-81`), the factory centralizes defaults, and the two pages embed one `pending-invites` component. But the e-mail is normalized three times (`Members.php:62`, `EntityInvite.php:56-60`, `PendingInvites.php:27`, `:92`), the `pending` scope is re-implemented by hand inside the invite transaction (`Members.php:111-117`), and the catch-all `catch (QueryException)` (`:124`) treats any DB failure as a duplicate invite.

readability.evidence: Names are clear and methods are mostly focused, but `resources/views/emails/entity-invite.blade.php:13` leaves a debug-style raw date line (`format('d/m/Y') (format('Y-m-d'))`) immediately after the translated expiry line at `:12`, so every invite shows the date twice; `sendInvite()` is a single ~90-line method mixing validation, lookups, throttling, transaction and mail (`Members.php:56-143`); `ui.name`/`ui.email` headers at `members.blade.php:70-71` are inconsistent with the newly added `ui.invite_email`/`ui.invite_role`.

scope.evidence: Almost everything serves the task (model, migration, factory, mail, both components, both page integrations, nav visibility at `resources/views/layouts/default-page.blade.php:45`). Extras: an unrequested `admin()` factory state (`database/factories/EntityInviteFactory.php:40-45`) and a public `closeMember()` method not in the contract (`Members.php:225`), plus deletion of accepted invites, which the task does not ask for.

issues.explanation: The entire feature ships without a single Pest/PHPUnit test, including the mandatory unauthorized-call and tamper tests for each new Livewire action.

The invite form renders no `@error('inviteEmail')` element (only `@error('inviteRole')` at :29), yet `sendInvite()` reports already-member, already-invited and rate-limit failures on `inviteEmail` (Members.php:78, :89, :98), so the required single `help is-danger` message is missing and users get no feedback when an invite is rejected.

Invite creation and acceptance are domain writes performed inline in Livewire components instead of the project's one-action-per-use-case `app/Actions/*` classes, which conventions.md:42-45 mandates for domain writes.

A new table and a new domain rule (invite-only membership) are not reflected in `docs/database-schema.md`, `docs/business-rules.md` or `CHANGELOG.md`, which conventions.md:92-103 requires in the same change.

The task requires employees to get a 403 from the `entity.members` route as well as the component; no route middleware/guard is added, so only the component's `mount()` authorization (`Members.php:51`) covers it.
The replace step deletes rows with `accepted_at` not null, but the task only allows replacing an expired invite; this silently destroys accepted-invite history and goes beyond the specified rule.

Opening the owner's membership prefills `memberRole` with `owner`, which fails the `admin,employee` validation before `abort_if($membership->role === UserRole::Owner, 403)`, so the specified 403 is unreachable from the UI (and the select at members.blade.php:112-114 shows 'Admin' while the state is 'owner').
A leftover raw-date line renders the expiry date a second time after the translated line, producing duplicated/garbled output in every invite e-mail.
New user-facing errors are passed as untranslated English keys and are not added to `lang/pt_BR.json`, so pt_BR managers see English messages.
Validation uses an inline rules array; the project pattern is `#[Validate]` attributes plus `$this->validate()`, and this change even removes the existing `#[Validate]` import.
`ui.name` and `ui.email` are used but not added to `lang/en/ui.php`/`lang/pt_BR/ui.php` in this diff (the previous views used `__('Name')`/`__('E-mail')`), so these headers may render the raw key.

Mass-assignment protection uses the `#[Fillable]` attribute (and its class import at :5) instead of the `$fillable` property used by sibling models; with composer.json absent from the diff, support in the installed Laravel version cannot be verified.
Invites are looked up globally with `findOrFail` before the e-mail check, so 404 vs 403 discloses whether a given invite ID exists.
Catching every `QueryException` and reporting 'already invited' masks unrelated database failures (e.g. a failing delete or FK error) as a duplicate invite.
An `admin()` factory state and a public `closeMember()` method are added although neither is asked for in the task or contract.

review.summary: The change implements invite-only membership end to end: the `entity_invites` table/model/factory, a queued mailable and pt_BR copy, a `PendingInvites` component wired into switcher and onboarding, and a manager-only members page with invite form, pending list, member modal and removal confirmation. The main blockers are that the whole feature ships with no tests, the invite form never renders the `inviteEmail` validation error, and the domain writes bypass the project's Actions layer; docs and CHANGELOG are also untouched. Requirements are mostly present, security looks sound, but the gaps plus the absent test suite mean substantial rework before merge.
